paragraphs.text: The congenital dyserythropoietic anemias are a heterogeneous group of rare disorders that primarily affect erythropoiesis. They show characteristic morphologic abnormalities and a block in erythroid maturation. Mutations in the CDAN1 gene cause most cases of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. In about 20% of cases no likely pathogenic CDAN1 mutation is found, and some of these cases are caused by mutation in C15ORF41 (Babbs et al., 2013).

paragraphs.text: Sabry et al. (1997) described dysmorphic features in 3 Bedouin sibs with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. The features were growth retardation/short stature, congenital ptosis, abnormal tarsal bones, metatarsal duplication/hypoplasia, nail/phalangeal hypoplasia of the fingers and toes, Madelung deformity, syndactyly of the toes, and hallux valgus. Peripheral blood lymphocyte cultures from the patients had a very low mitotic index. The phenotype varied among the 3 sibs. Sabry et al. (1997) concluded that their report confirmed an association between a subset of congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I and a specific form of distal limb anomalies. They suggested that congenital ptosis and a low mitotic index might also be part of the syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Babbs et al. (2013) studied a consanguineous pedigree of Middle Eastern origin with congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type I. Using whole-genome sequencing and segregation analysis, they identified a homozygous c.533T-A transversion in the C15ORF41 gene, a gene of unknown function. The change was predicted to cause a leu178-to-gln (L178Q) substitution. They then sequenced C15ORF41 in other CDAN1 mutation-negative pedigrees with the disorder. In 2 further pedigrees of Southeast Asian origin, they found a homozygous c.281A-G transition that was predicted to cause a tyr94-to-cys (Y94C) substitution. The haplotype surrounding c.281A-G suggested a founder effect for this mutation in Pakistan. Sequence similarity searches indicated that C15ORF41 encodes a novel restriction endonuclease of the Holliday junction resolvase family.

agent.process_note: I read all 4 files in full. Two are abstracts only (Sabry et al., 1997; Babbs et al., 2013). The two Ahmed et al. (2006) papers are titles only, so I used them only for the heterogeneity statement that their titles support. The causal gene (C15ORF41), the zygosity (homozygous) and both variants come from the Babbs et al. (2013) abstract. No reference data were supplied, so the intro gives no gene MIM number or chromosomal location. The Sabry et al. (1997) family (3 Bedouin sibs with CDA I and distal limb anomalies) was not genotyped in that abstract, so it is not linked to C15ORF41 here. The abstracts give no numbers of affected individuals per pedigree, ages or functional assays, and I wrote none.
